thread:
maria: Heads up — on the sampleapp onboarding tests I'm seeing a weird cascade: auth refreshs + paginated list calls cause client-side throttle spikes. Not full 429s from API, but our SDK backoff kicks in and stalls the paginator. Anyone seen this?

kevin: hmm, is that the new prefetch paginator?

maria: yes, the one with adaptive windowing. repro steps: start 8 parallel sessions, each iterates pages with pageSize=50. Token refresh happens ~5s in. After refresh the per-client concurrency window drops to 1 for a short time and all sessions queue up.

maria: paste of a small log snippet:
```
[2026-03-20T15:02:11Z] fetchPage(session=3,page=4) -> 200 (latency 120ms)
[2026-03-20T15:02:16Z] token:refresh(session=3) -> 200
[2026-03-20T15:02:16Z] client-window.adjust(session=3) new=1 old=6 reason=token_refresh
[2026-03-20T15:02:16Z] enqueue(session=1,page=5) wait=3.2s
```

dan: whoa new=1 old=6? that change looks like an overly conservative reset. SDK should decay window more gently on auth events.

kevin: agreed — current heuristic clamps to 1 on ANY auth hiccup to be safe. sounds like we need a smoother cooldown and maybe avoid clamping when upstream 200s continue.

elaine: what about pagination state? If the paginator sees repeated short queues we sometimes re-initialize cursor backoff. Could be compounding.

maria: exact problem: auth refresh transient => window clamp to 1 => prefetch buffer empties => paginator sees emptiness and triggers aggressive prefetch (more requests) which then get queued by clamp => thundering retry-like pattern. end result: perceived stall for ~6–9s.

dan: sounds like a control-loop oscillation. Two quick ideas: (1) on auth refresh, don't drop below 25% of previous window unless we actually see 429/503 from server. (2) keep prefetch buffer target proportional to active window so buffer doesn't overcompensate.

kevin: +1. we should add a safety: if token refresh succeeded with 2xx and immediate downstream requests are healthy (<5% errors) then fast-path restore to previous window with jittered ramp rather than clamp.

ci-bot: Deployment note: opened issue #INFR-6123 "sdk: reduce clamp on auth refresh to avoid pagination stalls" and attached logs from maria.

elaine: can we reproduce reliably in CI? maybe add a test that forces token refresh mid-iteration and asserts no >3s stall.

maria: I can add a deterministic integration test that manipulates token TTL and simulates 8 sessions. Will submit a draft PR later today.

dan: also flag for docs: in onboarding guide mention that token rotation interacts with client-side backpressure and recommend token lifetime > 30s for heavy pagination.

kevin: good call. I'll open a small PR for the heuristic change and add a comment to the adaptive window code.

maria: thanks — I'll drop the test PR link once ready.

kevin: once PRs land let's run a smoke with sampleapp load generator (link: https://ci.internal/redwood/sampleapp-load) and watch the dashboard. If we still see stalls we can add a tunable env var for the clamp threshold. :mag:

maria: noted. thanks all :party_parrot:
